value.body: Technical writers produce manuals, help guides, API documentation and release notes that explain products and software. They work in software companies, engineering and manufacturing firms and documentation service providers, and the day involves learning a product, talking to engineers and writing and editing content.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BA (English), B.Tech or B.Sc; strong writing is the main requirement

items.label: Common tools
items.value: MS Word, Markdown, Confluence, MadCap Flare or similar authoring tools

items.label: Tech industry workforce
items.note: Direct employees across India's IT and tech-services industry at the end of FY 2024-25, with ~1.3 lakh added that year; covers all roles, not this role alone

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often enter through writing tests at software firms or documentation service companies; a portfolio of sample documents (a how-to guide, a product manual) carries weight. Basic technical knowledge of the product area makes the work easier.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Editing and following a style guide
Working with engineers and product teams

value.title: At a glance
items: Software and API documentation usually needs more technical depth than general content writing.
Common next steps: senior writer, documentation lead, or content design.
AI writing tools are changing the job towards editing and information design.
